fields.mechanism: Magnetostatic suspension and control of a rotor eliminates mechanical contact, thereby decoupling rotational dynamics from lubricant viscosity and thermal contraction effects.
fields.intervention: Replace the ball bearings with a closed-loop magnetic bearing system that is thermally isolated from the radiator, maintaining a constant gap and damping characteristic independent of ambient temperature.
fields.expected_effect: The bearing stiffness and damping remain constant across the thermal cycle, preventing the loss of clearance or stick-slip friction that causes intermittent stall during shadowing.
fields.falsification_test: Perform a low-temperature spin-up test on the ground prototype by cooling the bearing housing to the target shadow temperature while monitoring current draw; a magnetic bearing will show no spike in torque required to maintain speed, whereas a failing mechanical bearing will show increased resistance.

fields.mechanism: Magnetic bearing suspension eliminates mechanical contact and lubricant viscosity dependence at low temperature.
fields.intervention: Command the existing wheel motor drive electronics to apply a controlled DC bias current profile that magnetically unloads the bearing preload, simulating magnetic bearing levitation without hardware modification.
fields.expected_effect: Removing mechanical contact eliminates the viscous drag increase of solidified or thickened lubricant, preventing intermittent stall during eclipse thermal transients.
fields.falsification_test: On-orbit, command the reaction wheel motor driver to inject a constant DC bias current offset into the phase windings during orbital shadow passage to magnetically unload the bearing; if the stall persists identically with and without the bias current, the lubricant-viscosity coupling hypothesis is falsified.
